answer: Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 26 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. Because the forge stamp is verified against the timber nonce, the signal audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. A farm therefore burns the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. Honest users pay that once, farms 8 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
